all_of: a login sets a cookie that is a base64 pickle of an application object
the server loads that cookie on later requests
an authenticated feature compiles user-supplied LaTeX
any_of: only an attribute such as authenticated is checked for access
the LaTeX input is filtered by a literal blacklist

chain.action: log in and decode the session cookie; a base64 value starting with gASV is a Python pickle
chain.why: the cookie is the trust boundary: the server deserialises it on later requests

chain.action: unpickle the cookie, set the authentication attribute to true, re-pickle and send it back
chain.why: the server type-checks the object but trusts its attributes, so forging them crosses the auth check

chain.action: map the authenticated feature; here it compiles LaTeX and serves the result at a predictable static path
chain.why: the flag lives in a file the LaTeX engine can read

chain.action: if a literal blacklist blocks LaTeX syntax, encode the whole document as ^^xx hex escapes
chain.why: TeX expands ^^xx after the filter has run, and the caret is not filtered

chain.action: use the verbatim-input LaTeX command to inline the flag file into the PDF, then fetch the PDF and read its text layer
chain.why: verbatim input needs no shell escape or \input

first_confirming_probe.request: log in with any username and base64-decode the resulting user cookie
first_confirming_probe.expected: the decoded bytes start with a pickle protocol header and reference an application class with an authentication attribute
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: the cookie is opaque or signed, so no object attributes are attacker-controlled

blast_radius: forging the cookie only changes your own session; the generated PDF is written to a fixed static path and must be overwritten with a benign document afterwards so the flag is not left on the shared instance

verification.evidence: the flag was extracted from the text layer of /static/input.pdf on the live target after the ^^xx LaTeX payload read the flag file

reuse_when: a session cookie decodes to a pickle (gASV / gAJ prefix)
a feature compiles LaTeX or another document format from user input
a filter blocks literal characters but not an encoding the downstream tool expands
known_traps: the __reduce__ pickle RCE may be blocked by an object type check; attribute forgery is the working route
the naive \input{|cmd} payload is blocked by a literal blacklist; use ^^xx escapes
the generated PDF persists at a fixed path; overwrite it after reading the flag
the flag file is relative to the application directory
